findings.title: Create a fresh queue pool for each processing strategy
findings.body: The factory creates one queue pool in its constructor and reuses it for every create_with_partitions call, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close shuts that pool down. Arroyo closes and recreates strategies when partition assignments change, so after the first rebalance the new strategy receives queues whose workers have stopped and whose queues have been shut down. Submissions then fail and the submit exception handler marks those messages completed, allowing unprocessed results to be committed. The pool and its offset tracker need a lifecycle scoped to each strategy rather than being reused after shutdown.

findings.title: Bound queued work and propagate backpressure
findings.body: Every worker queue is created with the default maxsize=0, which makes it unbounded, and submit always accepts more work. If processing is slower than Kafka ingestion, or a worker is blocked on a slow result, the consumer continues accumulating decoded results, original Kafka messages, and offset-tracking entries in memory without limit. This can exhaust the consumer's memory instead of applying the advertised backpressure. Use bounded capacity and signal Arroyo to retry submissions when capacity is exhausted.

findings.title: Drain accepted work and commit completion before graceful shutdown
findings.body: close stops the commit loop before shutting down the pool, and pool shutdown sets every worker's shutdown flag before draining its queue. Consequently, queued results are abandoned and results completed during worker shutdown are never included in a final commit. join simply calls close again and ignores its timeout, so it does not provide Arroyo's graceful draining phase either. On shutdown or rebalance this causes accepted work to be replayed, including already-applied results; workers that exceed the fixed five-second join can also keep applying old results after processing resumes elsewhere. Separate closing submissions from draining workers, honor the join timeout, and commit the final completed offsets after draining.

findings.title: Do not acknowledge messages when submission fails
findings.body: The broad submit exception handler treats any decoding, grouping, or enqueueing exception as successful completion by adding and immediately completing the message's offset. For example, if build_payload_grouping_key raises or work_queue.put fails because the queue is shut down, the result was never handed to a worker but the next commit can advance past it permanently. Expected invalid-payload handling already has the decoder's None path; unexpected submission failures should propagate or remain pending rather than acknowledge unprocessed results.
